answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by completing tasks whose results are later checked against independently sampled ground truth; repeated identities do not multiply credit, because each accepted result is tied to a costly, nontransferable stake that is slashed when wrong. A canyon of fake accounts therefore needs real capital and useful, verifiable work, not just cheap registrations. The prism of independent checks makes coordinated errors visible, while a ridge of accumulated reputation raises the cost of replacing exposed identities.
